(1) small groups of pedestrians can be detected in videos of crowds, and (2) these groups are often elongated and oriented in the direction of motion

(1) we can reliably detect small groups in crowds using a novel clustering approach, (2) the groups we detect are statistically consistent with human perception of small groups, and (3) the shape of these groups can be described by an underlying statistical model.

(a) we present the first automated approach to detecting small groups in crowded pedestrian scenes, (b) we validate our approach using human-coded ground truth and show that our approach is able to detect small groups with high accuracy, and (c) our results reveal patterns of pedestrian group structure that complement current research on crowd dynamics and may have applications in crowd modeling and real-time situation analysis.
